newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--There is a significant difference in views between the national economy and labour ministries on employment and social security issues. The breach appeared at yesterday's meeting chaired by National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou: two committees will be set up to find common ground for the government, ahead of social dialogue.
--Two Olympic Airways flights were cancelled yesterday and delays noted in an ominous precursor to events after pilots and adminisitration disagreed over working guidelines.
--Although inflows into mutual fund shares so far have been unimpressive, the near future is expected to bring a more impressive performance.

--The government is mobilising its union affiliates in an effort to stave off strike action before it begins, in the light of the beginning of dialogue on sector labour agreements and changes to social security and employment.
--The Bank of Greece has also come out with optimistic prospects for a GDP growth rate of above 3.0 percent for this year, and inflation close to 4.5 percent by the end of the year.
--The national economy ministry will today host a meeting on the final form the OTE (Greece telecoms organisation) share offer will take. KERDOS
--The central bank and the finance ministry is now considering putting a brake on the further drop in interest rates but in April, when inflation has fallen significantly.

--Deputy Finance Minister George Drys yesterday announced the inclusion of judicial officials in the new economic crimes squad, saying the new body would be the immediate and active supporter of justice and a revolutionary measure in combatting economic crimes.
--A further fall in inflation this month and next presages well for the wholesale price index for January.

--The development ministry is planning serious fines for those who sell their products below cost and for misleading advertising. Services at the ministry also said yesterday that customs checks were not enough to guarantee quality of imported items.
--The government is expected to firm up its positions in the next few days, ahead of the social dialogue with unionists, employers and producers. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
